verses.text: Now, brothers and sisters, about spiritual gifts: I don't want you to be uninformed.
You remember that when you were Gentiles, you were led astray to worship idols that can't speak, however you were influenced.
So I want you to know: no one speaking by God's Spirit says, ‘Jesus is cursed,’ and no one can say, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit gives them.
There are different kinds of service, but the same Lord is served.
There are different kinds of work, but the same God empowers everyone in every way.
The Spirit's presence is given to each person for the good of all.
To one, the Spirit gives a message of wisdom; to another, a message of knowledge, by the same Spirit.
To another, faith by the same Spirit; to another, gifts of healing by that one Spirit.
To another, miraculous powers; to another, prophecy; to another, the ability to discern spirits; to another, different kinds of languages; and to another, the interpretation of languages.
One and the same Spirit brings all of this about, giving each person gifts as he chooses.
Just as one body has many parts, and all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ.
We were all baptized by one Spirit into one body—Jews or Greeks, enslaved or free—and we were all given the same Spirit to drink.
The body isn't made up of one part, but many.
If the foot says, ‘I'm not a hand, so I don't belong to the body,’ that doesn't make it any less part of the body.
And if the ear says, ‘I'm not an eye, so I don't belong to the body,’ that doesn't make it any less part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, how would it hear? If the whole body were an ear, how would it smell?
But God arranged every part in the body exactly as he wanted it.
If all the parts were the same, where would the body be?
As it is, there are many parts but one body.
The eye can't tell the hand, ‘I don't need you!’ And the head can't tell the feet, ‘I don't need you!’
On the contrary, the parts that seem weaker are necessary.
The parts we think less honorable we treat with greater honor, and the parts we consider less presentable get special care,
while the presentable parts don't need extra care. God put the body together and gave greater honor to the parts that lacked it,
so there would be no division in the body, but that all the parts would care equally for one another.
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it. If one part is honored, every part celebrates with it.
You are Christ's body, and each of you is a part of it.

God has appointed people in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then those who do miracles, those with gifts of healing, those who help, those who lead, and those who speak different languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in different languages? Do all interpret?
Eagerly seek the greater gifts. And now I'll show you a way that's far better.
